newsitem.title: MEXICO: GMexico Q1 net seen down on copper prices.
newsitem.headline: GMexico Q1 net seen down on copper prices.

text.p: Mexican copper giant Grupo Mexico (GMexico) is expected to see a decline in net earnings in the first quarter from the year-ago period because of lower copper prices, analysts said.

Analysts said the first quarter will look better than the fourth quarter as world copper prices have recovered somewhat. But the first quarter will suffer compared to the year-ago period, as copper prices have yet to regain those levels, they added.
A Reuters survey of four analysts forecast the company's earnings for the first three months of the year would be 0.92 peso per share versus 1.204 in December 1996 pesos.

"They should have a good quarter (compared to the fourth quarter) because of higher metal prices," Serfin brokerage analyst Hector Novoa said. "In terms of margin, we expect a drop even compared to the last quarter (from 28.5 to 25.1 percent), mainly because of taxes."
Higher production in the quarter was offset by a stable peso, despite inflation of about five percent in the period, analysts said. GMexico's sales are heavily weighted in dollars.

"I believe they should have rather favorable results for the first half, so long as copper prices don't fall much," Novoa added. Higher zinc and silver prices will also be key to the company's earnings, he added.
Paribas analyst Nigel Kieser said the company's expansions at its La Caridad unit should have been at full capacity for the quarter.
"The company's new smelter and refinery should be ready any day now," Credit Lyonnais analyst David Bodenberg noted. Both are being built by Bufete Industrial.

Analysts said trade in GMexico stock has remained sluggish because of U.S. ASARCO's continued inability to sell its 23.6 percent stake in the company. Negotiations between the two companies have so far been fruitless, and the stock overhang has hurt Grupo Mexico, analysts said.
The company's bidding for the Pacific-North railway line could help GMexico secure the best costs and transportation to its key copper facilities in northern Chihuahua state, analysts said.

Grupo Mexico is one of three bidders for the more than 6,000 km railroad, expected to attract bids of about $1 billion. The company is reportedly in talks with competing Tribasa to join forces in a bid.
